recent: Thu 24 Sep · 18:19: Tomas finished a campfire.
Thu 24 Sep · 18:39: Tomas stopped and thought: “Fire's holding. Get the lean-to walls up before dark takes the warmth with it — one task, then the next, same as before.”

Fri 25 Sep · 05:30: Baby rabbits appeared near the meadow.
Fri 25 Sep · 06:36: A scruffy stray dog appeared at the edge of the forest.
Fri 25 Sep · 06:57: Tomas learned something. He's learned to handle thorny plants.
Fri 25 Sep · 07:44: Tomas stopped and thought: “Cockles under the sand, mussels on the rocks. The sea pays rent twice a day.”
Fri 25 Sep · 07:59: Tomas stopped and thought: “Tide's turning, pockets full. Time to feed the fire and start hauling wood — the walls won't build themselves before the rain does.”
Fri 25 Sep · 08:03: He found the fire had gone out.
Fri 25 Sep · 08:03: He has no shelter yet, whatever he tells himself.
Fri 25 Sep · 09:58: Tomas set himself a plan: rebuild the fire and finish the lean-to.

hisNotes: day 1: The fire took most of the evening and nearly didn't catch — don't let it go out if you can help it. Walk to that lake once there's a roof over your head.
day 1: Day one: fire's alive, I'm alive. Feed it before you sleep, not after you wake up scared. Walls next, then the lake.
day 2: The fire held the whole night. That dog is still out there watching. Don't let the tide turn you lazy—work while the rocks are bare.
day 2: Tide's turned — no more shellfish till it's out again. Today's work: feed the fire, haul wood, get the first walls up before the weather turns.
day 2: You told yourself the fire was still burning. It wasn't. Stop assuming. Go and look. Walls and roof before nightfall, or you're spending another night in the damp cold.
hisGoals: Keep the fire alive, always (since day 1)
Get walls and a roof over my head (since day 1)
Find that lake and fresh water (since day 1)
Learn what this island can give me (since day 1)

memories.what: Saw a dog today! Skinny, scruffy, watching me from the trees. How did it get here?
Thorns ripped my hands to bits. Gloved in a scrap of cloth now, and I lift the canes with a stick.
Fire! I got a real fire going. I sat and watched it for an hour.
Cockles under the sand, mussels on the rocks. The sea pays rent twice a day.
Walked back and the fire was out. Cold ashes. I'd been telling myself it was still burning.
One more night exposed like this could cost me the fire and the warmth both. Shelter comes before anything clever.
Saw tiny rabbits by the meadow today. Spring's here.
Fire's holding. Get the lean-to walls up before dark takes the warmth with it — one task, then the next, same as before.
Built a lean-to out of branches and grass. It leaks a little, but it's mine.
No roof over my head yet. I have to stop pretending and build one.
Fire's out and I wasted half the morning. Shelter and heat before the fog turns to rain.
